first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this with 'Mum, look at Santorini!'. The first paragraph talks about guest numbers and 'how those guests will travel', not just pretty views, so I'm reading on. Sensible, grown-up tone. The big table is a lot on the iPad, but the venue sections are short and tidy.

journey.quote: Curfews, minimum nights and rain plans are rarely published, so have them confirmed in writing before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone finally says 'in writing' and 'deposit' in the same breath. That's exactly what I'd tell her.

journey.section: Greece wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Region | Type | Ceremony on site | Exclusive use | Largest published capacity |
journey.reaction: Six columns and twenty rows is fiddly on the iPad, and there's no column for whether Nana can actually get around the place. I'll come back to it on the computer.

journey.section: How to compare Greece wedding venues like for like
journey.quote: For Australian guest lists, rooms on site matter more than usual. Guests who have flown a long way stay several nights, and fewer transfers mean an easier week for everyone.
journey.reaction: Yes. My mother and my aunts are not hopping in and out of minibuses every day. This is the kind of thinking I want.

journey.quote: Published ceremony spaces in Oia and Imerovigli seat 20 to 60, so a Santorini cliff-edge wedding suits a smaller guest list.
journey.reaction: Well, that settles a few arguments in our house. We have more than 60 on Dad's side alone.

journey.quote: [Grace Hotel](https://auberge.com/grace-hotel/events/weddings/) is a clifftop hotel above the caldera, where the ceremony can include a unity rite mixing black and white volcanic sand, 363 metres above sea level.
journey.reaction: Clifftop, split-level terraces. Lovely photos, I'm sure, but my mother uses a walking frame. Not one Santorini entry says anything about steps, lifts or level access.

journey.quote: Valet parking, access for guests with special needs, a room for the couple and a generator.
journey.reaction: That's the only venue in the whole list that mentions access at all, and it's the one with no bedrooms. I noticed.

journey.quote: For a guest list flying in from Australia, the Riviera has one clear advantage: the airport is close.
journey.reaction: Twenty minutes from the airport. After a 24-hour flight at my mother's age, that matters more than any view.

journey.section: Getting there from Australia: flights, ferries and transfers
journey.quote: As at November 2026, services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly because of strong winds, and passengers usually carry their own luggage up and down stairs.
journey.reaction: Thank you for being honest. That one line rules out an island for half our relatives. I'll be showing my husband this.

journey.section: When to marry in Greece: season, heat and the meltemi
journey.quote: It notes that wildfires occur from June to September, near cities and tourist areas on the mainland and the islands, and that heatwaves are frequent through summer.
journey.reaction: Quoting Smartraveller rather than some blogger. Good. Heat is a real worry with elderly guests, and the evening ceremony advice is sensible.

journey.section: Getting legally married in Greece as Australians, in brief
journey.quote: Which documents does the town hall need, and must they carry an apostille and an official Greek translation?
journey.reaction: A proper checklist. It does make me wonder who reads the venue contract if it's in Greek and in euros, though. That isn't covered.

journey.section: Shortlist your Greek venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing, AUD, one person start to finish. That's what I want to hear. I'd still want to speak to that person on the phone before we pay anything.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have level access, lifts or few steps from rooms to the ceremony and reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
Are deposits paid to Greek venues protected, and who holds them?
Is the venue contract in English, and is it priced in euros or Australian dollars once we sign with the venue itself?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Greek time?
Is the first step a phone call with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked?
What travel or medical insurance should older guests have for a Greek summer wedding?
would_share_with: My husband, with the ferry line and the Athens Riviera airport distances marked
My daughter, with the Santorini capacity numbers, gently
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the heat and evening ceremony section

cta_reaction.quote: With Wedded Concierge, you work with one Wedded Advisor from start to finish, in your time zone and quoting in AUD.
cta_reaction.why: One named person, AUD quotes and the fee in writing tick most of my boxes. I'd click if it's clear a real person rings me before anything is booked, and if they can tell me which venues suit my mother's mobility.

top_3_changes: Add accessibility to the 'Not published' line or 'Worth knowing' for each venue (steps, lifts, level paths), and flag the clifftop Santorini venues as hard going for guests with limited mobility.
In the closing section, say plainly that the first step is a phone conversation with the Wedded Advisor, before anything is booked or paid.
In the comparison or legal section, add one line on venue contracts and deposits: ask what language and currency the contract is in and how the deposit is held.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details and unprinted prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Venue accessibility for elderly guests is this persona's main content gap; deposit protection and on-the-day contact are business details and deferred. Treat accessibility as should-fix?

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
